_what: THE video names. Six lists: production format, style and script format on every ad; hook format and headline format only when the opening is made differently from the body. Every page, brief and run of the video line (teardown, writing, production, edit) uses these names, spelled exactly like this. Locked: a change needs the owner's own word, and formats/test_names.py fails on any change made without updating it. Plain words go beside a name ('what'), never in place of it.
signed: 2026-11-19, owner: "hold this naming list, do not change it ever again"; 2026-11-19, owner on the formats page: added Meme, Dramatic continuation, Micro-drama, Testimonial montage, Era roll call as script formats ("Add it" on D1-D5); 2026-11-19, owner: hook formats (the scroll stoppers) added as a fourth list, Dramatic continuation moved there from script format ("Yes, add those 4"); 2026-11-19, owner: "green screen reaction is a hook format, dramatized object is a hook format, street interview could be a script format"; 2026-11-19, owner: "how to get rid of chapped lips … that's just a demonstration script format with a up close body part hook format" (Up close body part added; id from the variations tool's first-frame list); 2026-11-19, the session decided on the owner's rules and he reviews (owner: "try to answer your own question before asking me"): 3 hook formats, 5 script formats, the headline format list (17), length Short/Long; 2026-11-21, owner on the Preset Library page: "Yes, add all 4" (Claymation, Needle felt, Art toy, Cinematic live action added to style; the first three keep their element-bank ids)

names.name: Single presenter
names.what: One person to camera

names.name: Song ad
names.what: A song carries it

names.name: Narrator montage
names.what: One voice over shots, nobody talks on screen

names.name: Multi-speaker scene
names.what: Two or more people talking

names.name: Short movie
names.what: Acted, no words, music only

names.name: Text thread
names.what: A phone screen tells it

names.name: Meme
names.what: One swiped meme beat, the caption added at the edit

names.name: Micro-drama
names.what: Several characters in one set: a confrontation, a turn, an offer

names.name: Testimonial montage
names.what: One person, one line, many times over

names.name: Era roll call
names.what: 'If you grew up in the [decade] you remember…', ending on the one she still carries

names.name: Street interview
names.what: A host stops strangers in public and asks them questions or plays a quick game

names.name: Founder story
names.what: The founder tells why they made it: their own problem, the search, the product

names.name: Personal story, then the fix
names.what: One customer's own problem, what they tried, what finally worked

names.name: Tips, then the pitch
names.what: Useful tips or a warning first, then the product as the answer

names.name: Deal walkthrough
names.what: A voice runs through the stacked discounts and the deadline

names.name: Glow-up
names.what: Before and after to music: the change is the whole ad

hook_format.means: the scroll stopper: the first seconds, made differently from the body, ending where the pitch starts (optional: most ads open with the body itself)

names.name: VFX stunt
names.what: One impossible, obviously faked moment in real handheld footage, then straight to the pitch

names.name: Fake billboard stunt
names.what: A giant billboard comes alive on a real street and hands the product out

names.name: Dramatic continuation
names.what: Watch-bait drama that cuts to the sales pitch

names.name: Weird stunt, then the pitch
names.what: An attention toll that has nothing to do with the offer, then the reveal

names.name: Green screen reaction
names.what: A person cut out over someone else's clip or photo, reacting to it

names.name: Dramatized object
names.what: An everyday object made to act out the problem or the fix

names.name: Up close body part
names.what: The first frame is a close-up of the problem on the body (lips, a pimple, a bump), then the body starts

names.name: Swiped viral clip
names.what: A borrowed viral clip with a meme caption, then the pitch

names.name: Split screen
names.what: Two people side by side, or the demo beside the presenter, from the first frame

names.name: 3D body animation
names.what: A 3D body or character acts the problem out

headline_format.means: the WORDS in the first seconds (spoken or on screen), apart from the hook format, what you see first; optional (none = no words up top)

names.name: Question
names.what: Opens on a question to the viewer

names.name: Story open
names.what: Opens mid-story: "So I…"

names.name: Bold claim
names.what: Opens on a strong claim

names.name: Problem callout
names.what: Names the viewer's problem

names.name: Command interrupt
names.what: Tells the viewer to stop or do something

names.name: How-to promise
names.what: Promises how to fix it: "How to get rid of…"

names.name: Curiosity gap
names.what: Withholds the answer: "Nobody tells you this…"

names.name: Relatable moment
names.what: A moment the viewer knows from their own life

names.name: List promise
names.what: Promises a list: "3 things…"

names.name: Result first
names.what: Opens on the result

names.name: Skit line
names.what: A character's line inside a staged scene

names.name: Song lyric
names.what: The first words are sung or rapped

names.name: Label text
names.what: The only words are an on-screen title or label

names.name: Regret open
names.what: Opens on a regret or apology

names.name: Reaction line
names.what: A live reaction to a clip

names.name: POV caption
names.what: An on-screen "POV:" line

names.name: Comment reply
names.what: Opens as a reply to a viewer's comment

length.means: how long it runs; a VSL is not a format, it is Long (owner, 2026-11-19)

names.name: Short
names.what: 2 minutes or under

names.name: Long
names.what: Over 2 minutes (what used to be called a VSL)
